checkpoints.description: [1/1] Close a real delivery gap: the freeze status had no source in the game, so the shatter bonus and the heavy slow were unreachable. Adds the Rime Chanter (a frost caster that pulses a 1.4s freeze in a 210px radius every 3.2s, placed in Prism Gardens, the Frozen Choir and the Thunder Vault) and an ice ground hazard that freezes anything standing on it for 1.2s and drains after 9s; cold biomes roll ice instead of flame. updateGround now owns both mud and ice. Species count 105. Failing-first: tests/freezing-enemies.test.ts (7 cases).

impact_assessment.why: The player asked for frozen effects and freezing enemies, and burn and mud both had real sources while freeze existed only in tests.
impact_assessment.benefits: The shatter bonus becomes reachable in play, cold floors feel different from hot ones, and the freeze mechanic is no longer dormant.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: HazardKind gains ice and Enemy gains an optional chill timer; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: no saved shape change; balance: short, non-stacking freezes.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Short durations that refresh rather than stack, ice dealing no damage, a no-flame-on-frozen-floors check across four seeds, and a 7-case suite.

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Verified: Rime Chanter is a non-guardian species placed only on frost, crystal and storm sections; it freezes the walker on its pulse and the freeze lapses back to full speed. Frozen floors carry 6-13 ice patches and zero flame across eight seeds; an ice patch freezes then drains; ice never damages the walker. In Edge a Section 11 Frostbound Archive showed wall ice and floor patches, and standing on one set the HUD chip to Frozen. 1061 tests across 219 files, lint/typecheck/build clean.
Task 'freeze-sources' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Complete the music request without provider keys: src/audio/arrangement.ts holds the procedural fallback as pure data - ambient is a slow pad with sparse bells and no rhythm, battle is a distinct piece per biome with its own tempo (76-132bpm), an eight-step bass figure drawn from the scale, percussion positions inside a four-beat bar and a drive level. Sound.playAmbience reads it: battle keeps the pad quieter, raises the filter, shortens the bells and starts startRhythm (bass + rhythmHit percussion). Rendered Muse tracks still take precedence; calm audio is untouched to preserve the menu sound the player likes. Failing-first: tests/music-arrangement.test.ts (7 cases).

impact_assessment.why: The request asks for battle and out-of-battle music; with no provider keys the fallback only brightened a filter, so fights sounded like calm with the treble up.
impact_assessment.benefits: The shipped build satisfies the request with no rendered audio, every biome fights to a different figure, and the menu keeps the sound the player liked.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Sound gains a rhythm clock and new data module; dependency: none beyond WebAudio; concurrency: two interval clocks that must both stop; state: ambienceKey already keys on the mode.
impact_assessment.mitigation: One stop() that clears both clocks, a drive of 0 for calm so no rhythm is ever started there, pure-data tests, and an interval-count probe proving battle starts the second clock.

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Verified: all 16 biomes have ambient and battle specs; battle always has percussion, a bass figure, a drive above 0.25 and a faster tempo than calm, while calm has no rhythm at all; every biome's battle figure is unique; tempos sit in 40-160 bpm and all percussion sits inside a four-beat bar. 1068 tests across 220 files, lint/typecheck/build clean. In Edge the sound object switched ambienceKey through ruins:false, ruins:true, hive:true, hive:false, and an interval-count probe showed calm starting 1 clock and battle starting 2, so the battle layer really runs; 0 console errors.
Task 'battle-music-fallback' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: 7bd81b56bd533fdc2301c5e5ef494ba4acbca608

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Ship a real soundtrack with no provider keys: scripts/synthesize_music.py renders all 33 tracks from src/data/music.json into assets/music/ as mono 16-bit 22050Hz WAV loops using only the Python standard library (wave/math/array/random). Ambient is slow detuned drones with sparse pentatonic bells; battle is a per-biome bass ostinato with noise percussion, heartbeat thump and sparse lead at each biome's tempo; the guardian theme is a heavier 12s variant. Note tails wrap into the loop start so loops are seamless. Sound.playTrack now tries OGG, then MP3, then WAV via loadFirstTrack, so WAV-only shipping loads. Muse generation stays available for studio renders and takes precedence. Failing-first: tests/music-synth.test.ts (6 cases).

impact_assessment.why: Music only played if Muse tracks had been rendered, which needs provider keys, so the game shipped without a soundtrack and the player asked to use a synth.
impact_assessment.benefits: The game has 33 real music files with zero keys or dependencies, calm and battle differ per biome, and the set stays around 11 MB.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Sound gains loadFirstTrack and a new script; dependency: none (stdlib only); concurrency: an in-flight decode can race a track switch; state: about 11 MB of WAV assets enter the repo.
impact_assessment.mitigation: A supersede check before playback, a missing-URL memo, short 8s loops to bound size, a 25 MB test ceiling, and --verify to check every file is non-silent.

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Verified: scripts/synthesize_music.py rendered 33 WAV loops and --verify reports 33/33 playable with peaks near 29490; every manifest track ships a mono 16-bit PCM file 6-14s long, calm and battle renders differ byte-wise, and the whole set is about 11MB (under the 25MB ceiling). 1074 tests across 221 files, lint/typecheck/build clean. In Edge at 1280x720 the running game loaded ruins-ambient then ruins-battle, trackBuffers reached 2, and the memo recorded only the absent OGG/MP3 URLs, proving the WAVs play; 0 console errors.
Task 'synth-soundtrack' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: 172791504d298f320b056a1b3814c7faf28b0130

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Fix the music URL base: Vite serves publicDir (the assets folder) at the site root, so tracks are fetched as ./music/<id>.wav. The loader was asking for ./assets/music/..., which only worked in dev because the dev server also exposes the raw assets directory; the built game would have 404ed every track and silently fallen back to procedural music. musicUrls now defaults its base to '.' and the URL test pins ./music/... paths.

impact_assessment.why: Dev served the old path by accident, so the production build would have shipped without any of the 33 synthesized tracks.
impact_assessment.benefits: The soundtrack loads in both dev and the built game, so the shipped artefact actually has music.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: musicUrls default base changes; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: The URL test pins the exact paths and the fix was verified in a production preview and in dev.

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Verified: musicUrls now yields ./music/<id>.ogg|mp3|wav; a production preview served ./music/ruins-ambient.wav as 200 audio/wav and the game loaded ruins-ambient then ruins-battle into the decode cache, while the dev server loaded storm-battle the same way. 1074 tests across 221 files, lint/typecheck/build clean, 0 console errors in both dev and preview.
Task 'music-url-fix' completed successfully.
